subject.title: [bug]：Gateway pairing failure on Trim OS / TerraMaster NAS: WebSocket closes with code 1002 during device proof response

question: Should the Trim OS pairing failure be handled as a core Gateway diagnostic or compatibility fix, a Trim OS package/config-management fix, or held pending the missing protocol trace?
rationale: The next code change could affect Gateway authentication semantics or an external package manager, and the current evidence does not identify whether the 1002 comes from a stale client protocol range, malformed connect frame, or package-generated config state.

options.title: Collect protocol proof first
options.body: Ask for redacted Gateway logs around the close, exact client/Gateway/package versions, sanitized connect frame metadata, and the regenerated `openclaw.json` diff before changing auth or packaging behavior.

options.title: Fix core diagnostics if confirmed
options.body: If logs show a supported client is sending a malformed or opaque connect frame, improve Gateway diagnostics or compatibility in core while keeping auth fail-closed.

options.title: Route package regeneration externally
options.body: If the only remaining issue is `trim.openclaw` rewriting config, hand the config-management behavior to the package owner rather than changing core Gateway auth.

recommendation.title: Collect protocol proof first
recommendation.body: Ask for redacted Gateway logs around the close, exact client/Gateway/package versions, sanitized connect frame metadata, and the regenerated `openclaw.json` diff before changing auth or packaging behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses Gateway auth boundaries, release/update expectations, and package-owner routing, which fits the adjacent product/release ownership trail better than a narrow line-owner decision.
